'''John Bryce McLeod''', {{post-nominals|FRS|FRSE}}<ref name="rsbm">{{cite journal|last1=Hastings|first1=Stuart|title=John Bryce McLeod. 23 December 1929 — 20 August 2014|journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|year=2016|volume=62 |pages=381–407 |publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2015.0031|doi-access=free}}</ref> (23 December 1929 – 20 August 2014<ref name="rs">{{Cite web |title=Fellow details - McLeod; John Bryce (1929 - 2014) |author= |website=Royal Society |date= |access-date=20 October 2021 |url= https://catalogues.royalsociety.org/CalmView/Record.aspx?src=CalmView.Persons&id=NA5076&pos=3 }}</ref>) was a British mathematician, who worked on linear and nonlinear partial and ordinary differential equations.

==Life and education==
McLeod was born in Aberdeen, Scotland, on 23 December 1929.<ref name=rs/> He was educated at [[Aberdeen Grammar School]]; the [[University of Aberdeen]], where he took a first in Mathematics and Natural Philosophy in 1950; and [[Christ Church, Oxford]], where he took a first in Mathematics in 1952. He was a Harmsworth Senior Scholar at [[Merton College, Oxford]], from 1955 to 1956.<ref name="MCreg">{{cite book|editor1-last=Levens|editor1-first=R.G.C.|title=Merton College Register 1900–1964|date=1964|publisher=Basil Blackwell|location=Oxford|page=463}}</ref> He obtained his PhD in 1959 under the supervision of [[Edward Charles Titchmarsh]] at the University of Oxford.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=41774}}</ref>

He was a junior lecturer in Mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1956 to 1958, and a lecturer in mathematics at the [[University of Edinburgh]] from 1958 to 1960. He then returned to Oxford to take up a Fellowship in Pure Mathematics at [[Wadham College, Oxford|Wadham College]].<ref name="MCreg" /> He remained in Oxford until 1988, becoming a university lecturer in 1970, and a senior research fellow of the [[Science and Engineering Research Council]] from 1986 to 1991.<ref name="OxfordDNB">{{cite book |last1=Ball |first1=John |contribution=McLeod, John Bryce [known as J. Bryce McLeod] |url=https://www.oxforddnb.com/view/10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.001.0001/odnb-9780198614128-e-108577 |title=Oxford Dictionary of National Biography |publisher=Oxford University Press |doi=10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.013.108577 |isbn=978-0-19-861412-8 |access-date=12 January 2021}}</ref> In 1988 McLeod took up a professorship at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], where he remained until his retirement in 2007.<ref name="PittObit">{{Cite web |title=Emeritus Professor J. Bryce McLeod FRS Passes Away |author= |website=Department of Mathematics, University of Pittsburgh |date=9 September 2014 |url= https://www.mathematics.pitt.edu/news/emeritus-professor-j-bryce-mcleod-frs-passes-away}}</ref>

McLeod married Eunice Third in 1956; they had three sons and a daughter.<ref name="OxfordDNB" /> He died in England on 20 August 2014, aged 84.<ref name="PittObit" />

==Awards and honours==
In 1965, he was awarded the [[Sir Edmund Whittaker Memorial Prize]]. he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1974, and received the Society's [[Keith Medal]] in 1987.<ref name="OxfordDNB" /> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1992|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1992]].<ref name=rsbm/>

In 2011 he was awarded the [[Naylor Prize and Lectureship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners|title=List of LMS prize winners - NAYLOR PRIZE AND LECTURESHIP IN APPLIED MATHEMATICS|work=London Mathematical Society}}</ref>
